strengths_deep_dive: The Islamic Association of Arabi demonstrates efficient capital deployment toward its primary programs. In FY2024 filings, the charity directed a <cite id="3">96.2% program expense Ratio</cite> to its operations, comfortably beating the 75% industry benchmark and the peer median of 89.5%. Furthermore, third-party ratings from Charity Navigator assign the group an <cite id="9">overall rating of 81/100</cite>, backed by a perfect 100 score in Leadership.
rich_narrative.summary:
The Islamic Association of Arabi, operating as Masjid Yaseen, provides religious education and community support through its mosque and full-time academies. Founded in 1985, the organization has operated for over four decades, offering daily prayers, youth Islamic schooling, dawah work, and essential life services such as funeral and wedding support <cite id="1">in the local community</cite>.

Financially, the charity reported <cite id="2">$2,357,167 in revenue</cite> in fiscal year 2024 filings. Financial health metrics show a high commitment to direct spending, with a <cite id="3">96.2% program expense Ratio</cite> in FY2024 and an official Program ratio score based on a <cite id="9">96.2% program expense ratio</cite>. Fundraising costs are minimal, sitting at <cite id="9">less than one cent per dollar raised</cite>. The organization also maintains an overall <cite id="9">rating of 81.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>.

Despite these operational strengths, the organization exhibits critical governance and asset distribution gaps. Internal evaluations highlight weak board oversight and a lack of public board details. Additionally, the charity holds <cite id="9">38.8 months of working capital</cite> in reserves. For a zakat-collecting institution, accumulating nearly four years of operating reserves presents a significant concern regarding the prompt distribution of religious funds.
